messages:
incident-bot: ALERT: Elevated 5xx/error rate detected for model-serving runtime in us-west-2 (gateway). Error rate up ~18% vs baseline over last 5m. Dashboard: https://dash.redwood.ai/alerts/1788 (auto-escalation). Affected endpoints: /v1/generate, /v1/chat. Potential customer impact: increased latencies/timeouts and 502/504 responses.

emma: I'm on it. Paging @raj (runtime) and @alec (infra) — can someone confirm scope? Any initial customer reports? :pager:

marisol: Support: we've had 3 customer tickets in the last 10m for 502s/timeouts. Customers: AcmeHealth (payments flows), SketcherApp (chat). They've reported increased request failures and a few request retries.

raj: looking at model-runner logs right now. Seeing repeated segfaults and OOMs on a subset of pods. Example stack/log snippet:

```
2025-05-08T07:03:12Z model-runner[pid=2412]: ERROR SIGSEGV at 0x7ffd1f2c
2025-05-08T07:03:12Z kernel: [OOM] task model-runner invoked oom-killer: Out of memory: Killed process 2412 (model-runner)
2025-05-08T07:03:13Z model-runner[pid=2412]: RESTARTING due to panic: kv_cache overflow (seq_len=4096)
```

raj: hypothesis — a small percentage of requests with very long sequences (truncated prompts + embeddings) are causing KV cache growth and then allocator fragmentation -> OOM -> segfault. Reproduced locally on a dev node with a long sequence stress test.

alec: infra telemetry shows 6 pods restarted in the past 8m under the gpu-pool-usw2-1 autoscaling group. Memory usage trace attached: spike then crash. I can spin up extra nodes and drain the bad pods. Recommend immediate mitigation: 1) traffic split to safe model variant, 2) scale pool by +20% and cordon the nodes with repeated restarts.

emma: Agreed. Priorities: protect customers first (fallback/reroute), reduce blast radius (scale + cordon), collect artifacts for postmortem. @tim can you run fallback routing to small variant? I'll start the cordon/evict plan.

tim: Doing traffic shift now — will route 100% of incoming traffic for /v1/generate and /v1/chat to model:openai-like/sm-4k (cpu-backed) and set slow draining on current gpu pool. Command I used:

```
# route all production traffic off risky model
redwoodctl route update --selector endpoint=/v1/* --match-label=model=prod-large --set-model=open/model-sm-4k --timeout=30s
redwoodctl pool scale --pool=gpu-pool-usw2-1 --replicas=+3
```

tim: Routing change applied. Monitoring error rate and latency now.

incident-bot: ROUTE_UPDATE: traffic policy change executed by tim at 07:07 UTC. New policy: prod -> open/model-sm-4k (cpu) for matched endpoints.

raj: After routing we should see errors drop but higher latencies for some customers. I'm pushing a hotfix branch that adds early kv-cache eviction for sequences > 2048 and a safer allocator fallback (merged to canary). PR: https://git.redwood.internal/r/runtime/evict-kvcache-2048 (WIP). Will we canary it to 2 pods?

alec: Canary +2 pods in canary pool. Also cordoned three unstable nodes: gpu-node-17, gpu-node-19, gpu-node-21. I've collected dmesg and core dumps and pushed to the artifacts bucket s3://redwood-incidents/1788888888/.

liz: Customer success — I've sent quick-bullet updates to AcmeHealth and SketcherApp that we're mitigating, routed to fallback model, and expect a resolution within 30m. They've been advised to pause large-batch requests until we confirm stability.

emma: Good. Monitoring shows 5xx rate decreased from 18% -> 3% within 2 minutes of routing. Latency p50 increased +120ms for some endpoints but acceptable. We'll keep the fallback in place until runtime hotfix canary is validated.

raj: Canary logs look clean so far (no segfaults in canary pods). KVCACHE eviction logic seems to prevent runaway memory. I'm promoting hotfix to rolling deploy across the pool with a controlled max-unavailable=2. Deploy command:

```
redwoodctl deploy rollout --service=model-runner --image=runtime/hotfix-evict:20250508 --strategy=rolling --max-unavailable=2
```

tim: Rollout started. Keeping traffic on cpu fallback during rollout to avoid customer impact.

incident-bot: ONCALL HANDOFF: pagerduty notified backup oncall @emma-backup at 07:15 UTC due to extended mitigation.

marisol: Support: customers are acknowledging updates; a couple reported transient errors during the switch but no data loss. We'll keep monitoring tickets and escalate if any reopens.

emma: Action items captured: 1) raj to complete postmortem draft and root cause (kv cache + long-seq inputs + allocator frag). 2) infra (alec) to reintroduce drained nodes after validation. 3) support (marisol/liz) to notify affected customers with timeline and mitigation steps. 4) engineering to add request-size guardrails in API and alert on seq_len anomalies.

raj: I'll own the postmortem and include perf tests and a regression eval. ETA for initial draft: EOD today.

emma: Thanks all — keeping this thread for timeline notes. Will update status channel once we transition to postmortem. :thumbsup:
